set_aside.subject: REFUSAL_ANSWERS completeness and uniqueness
set_aside.text:
`REFUSAL_ANSWERS` holds exactly one row for each member of = models.RefusalCode, keyed by `code`; a
member without its row stops the build.
set_aside.question: Which module or build component verifies that every refusal code has exactly one row, when does it run, and does a duplicate row also stop the build?
options: The specification or code generator validates missing and duplicate rows before generating the service
`data_provider` validates the tuple when its module is imported
The deployment build validates the completed service artifact
Only the authored tuple is trusted; generated runtime code performs no validation
set_aside.default_guess: Have the specification or code-generation validator reject both missing and duplicate rows before service code is generated.

set_aside.subject: ownership of refusal status and detail values
set_aside.text: - the policy constants of A8, as typed values.
set_aside.question: Does `data_provider` own the code-to-status-and-detail decisions in `REFUSAL_ANSWERS`, or does it merely store decisions owned by `deliverer_api`, which says it owns the status and content of every refusal answer?
options: `data_provider` owns the fixed mapping values; `deliverer_api` owns only lookup and answer construction
`deliverer_api` owns the mapping decisions, while `data_provider` is only their storage mechanism
Split ownership explicitly: A8 owns the mapping values and A5/`deliverer_api` owns their application
set_aside.default_guess: Treat A8 and `data_provider` as owning the fixed mapping values, and narrow `deliverer_api` ownership to selecting the row and constructing the response.
